hesperosaurus:eswiki:4.title: Hesperosaurus mjosi (Osteodermos e impresiones de la piel)

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus is a herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur whose name means "western lizard" in Ancient Greek.
facts.quote: Hesperosaurus (from Ancient Greek ἕσπερος (hésperos), meaning "western", and σαῦρος (saûros), meaning "lizard") is a herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur

facts.statement: Fossils of Hesperosaurus have been found in Wyoming and Montana, USA, since 1985.
facts.quote: Fossils of Hesperosaurus have been found in the states of Wyoming and Montana in the United States of America since 1985

facts.statement: The species Hesperosaurus mjosi was named and described in 2001 by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward.
facts.quote: The type species Hesperosaurus mjosi was named and described in 2001 by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward

facts.statement: Fossil hunter Patrick McSherry discovered the remains of a stegosaur in Johnson County, Wyoming, in 1985.
facts.quote: In 1985, fossil hunter Patrick McSherry, at the ranch of S.B. Smith in Johnson County, Wyoming, found the remains of a stegosaur

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus back plates were likely shorter than those of Stegosaurus but longer.
facts.quote: The plates on its back were perhaps not as tall, but were longer

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus possibly had a deeper skull than Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: It possibly had a deeper skull than Stegosaurus

facts.statement: In 2015, additional specimens including at least five individuals were reported from quarries in Montana.
facts.quote: In 2015, additional specimens were reported: a concentration of at least five individuals discovered at the JRDI 5ES Quarry near Grass Range, Montana, and two individuals found in the Meilyn Quarry at Como Bluff

facts.statement: In 2010, Kenneth Carpenter rejected merging Hesperosaurus with Stegosaurus, arguing it was distinct enough to remain a separate genus.
facts.quote: Carpenter, considering the problem more of a philosophical than a scientific nature, in 2010 rejected the synonymy of Hesperosaurus with Stegosaurus stating that in his opinion Hesperosaurus was sufficiently different from Stegosaurus to be named a separate genus

facts.statement: In 2017, Raven and Maidment recognized Hesperosaurus as a genus distinct from Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2017, Raven and Maidment recognized both Miragaia and Hesperosaurus as genera distinct from Stegosaurus

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Hesperosaurus shows healed fractures, indicating it belonged to an older individual.
facts.quote: The skeleton was partly articulated and, in view of healed fractures, belongs to an old individual

facts.statement: A new specimen of Hesperosaurus mjosi was described from Montana in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, new specimen of H. mjosi was described from Montana

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus was a large stegosaur that reached 6.5 meters in length and 3.5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Hesperosaurus was a large stegosaur, reaching 6.5 m in length and 3.5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Some large individuals of Hesperosaurus may have reached 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Some large individuals may have reached 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Miles Carpenter provided the first formal diagnosis of Hesperosaurus in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001 Carpenter provided a diagnosis.

facts.statement: Maidment identified specific traits in Hesperosaurus that make it more evolutionarily basal than Stegosaurus armatus.
facts.quote: Maidment also provided some traits in which Hesperosaurus was more basal than Stegosaurus armatus.

facts.statement: The lower end of the pubic bone in Hesperosaurus is expanded and spoon-shaped when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: The lower end of the pubic bone is expanded (spoon-shaped in side view).

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus had twenty maxillary teeth per side, which is fewer than the number found in Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: The number of maxillary teeth were twenty per side, lower than the number with Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: The tail of Hesperosaurus ended with a thagomizer consisting of two pairs of spikes, with the front pair being thicker and the rear pair thinner and directed horizontally backward.
facts.quote: The end of the tail bore a "thagomizer" of two pairs of spikes, the front pair being thicker, the rear pair thinner and more horizontally directed to behind.

facts.statement: Rows of small hexagonal, non-overlapping, convex scales measuring two to seven millimeters in diameter were found on the lower trunk flank of Hesperosaurus.
facts.quote: A part of the lower trunk flank shows rows of small hexagonal, non-overlapping, convex scales, two to seven millimetres in diameter.

facts.statement: The discovery of a plate sheath impression in Hesperosaurus represents the first direct proof of such structures in any stegosaurian.
facts.quote: It is the first direct proof of such sheaths with any stegosaurian.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the presence of a sheath on Hesperosaurus plates indicates a primary defensive function, as the horn layer would have strengthened the plate and provided sharp cutting edges.
facts.quote: The study considered the presence of a sheath to be a strong indication that the plate had primarily a defensive function, as a horn layer would have strengthened the plate as a whole and provided it with sharp cutting edges.

facts.statement: A 2015 study by Evan Thomas Saitta concluded that Hesperosaurus exhibited sexual dimorphism based on finds from the JRDI 5ES Quarry.
facts.quote: In 2015, a study by Evan Thomas Saitta based on the finds in the JRDI 5ES Quarry concluded that Hesperosaurus showed sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Saitta suggested that tall back plates typified female Hesperosaurus, while males were equipped with low broad plates.
facts.quote: Saitta suggested that the tall plates typified the females, while the males were equipped with low plates.

facts.statement: The findings regarding sexual dimorphism in Hesperosaurus were questioned by paleontologists Kevin Padian and Kenneth Carpenter, though no formal scientific rebuttal was published.
facts.quote: The findings of the study were questioned by palaeontologists Kevin Padian and Kenneth Carpenter although no formal scientific studies were published as a rebuttal.

facts.statement: A 2001 cladistic analysis by Carpenter showed that Hesperosaurus was rather basal and related to Dacentrurus.
facts.quote: In 2001 Carpenter performed a cladistic analysis showing that Hesperosaurus was rather basal and related to Dacentrurus:

facts.statement: The genus Hesperosaurus was named by Carpenter, Miles, and Cloward in 2001.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Carpenter, Miles & Cloward, 2001

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Superior

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus mjosi was previously synonymized with Stegosaurus mjosi by Maidment and colleagues in 2008.
facts.quote: synonyms: Stegosaurus mjosi Maidment et al., 2008

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus lived approximately 152 million years ago during the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian stage in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 152 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Hesperosaurus to be 6.5 meters long and weigh 3.5 tons.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud en 6,5 metros, el peso en 3,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Maidment identified three unique traits: having thirteen rear vertebrae, an unfused fourth sacral vertebra, and rear plates that are longer than they are tall.
facts.quote: Maidment indicó tres autapomorfías, la posesión de once vértebras traseras, la cuarta vértebra sacra no se fusiona con el sacro, las placas traseras que son más largas, de adelante hacia atrás, que altas.

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus had twenty maxillary teeth on each side, which is fewer than the number found in Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: El número de dientes maxilares era veinte por lado, más bajo que el número con Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2007, Peter Malcolm Galton noted that Hesperosaurus teeth had vertical ridges on the crown and weakly developed fine grooves on the tooth surface.
facts.quote: Peter Malcolm Galton en 2007 estableció algunas diferencias: hay crestas verticales ásperas presentes en la parte superior de la corona, una por dentina; Los surcos finos en la superficie del diente están débilmente desarrollados.

facts.statement: In 2001, Carpenter identified ten plates in the holotype, describing them as long and low.
facts.quote: Carpenter en 2001 identificó diez placas como parte del holotipo. Los describió como largas y bajas.

facts.statement: The tail tip featured a thagomizer with two pairs of spikes, where the front pair was thicker and the rear pair was thinner and directed more horizontally backward.
facts.quote: El extremo de la cola tenía un Thagomizer de dos pares de puntas, el par delantero era más grueso, el par trasero más delgado y más horizontalmente dirigido hacia atrás.

facts.statement: A 2012 histological study concluded that Hesperosaurus osteoderms are structurally identical to those of Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2012, un estudio histológico concluyó que estos osteodermos, osificaciones de la piel, de Hesperosaurus son esencialmente idénticos en estructura a los de Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: Extensive long and wide arterial channels were observed in the bone structure of the plates.
facts.quote: Se observaron extensos canales arteriales largos y anchos.

facts.statement: This is the first direct evidence of horn sheaths on any stegosaur.
facts.quote: Es la primera prueba directa de tales envolturas con cualquier estegosáurido.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the horn sheath indicates a primarily defensive function, as it would have strengthened the plate and provided sharp edges.
facts.quote: El estudio consideró que la presencia de una vaina era un fuerte indicio de que la placa tenía principalmente una función defensiva, ya que una capa de cuerno habría fortalecido la placa en su conjunto y le habría proporcionado bordes afilados.

facts.statement: It is debated whether thermoregulation was possible for Hesperosaurus plates, as the horn sheath might have insulated them, though researchers note that cattle and ducks use horns to dissipate heat despite coverings.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, la termorregulación, otro rol a menudo asumido de las placas, se habría visto obstaculizada por una capa aislante adicional y la suavidad de la superficie, pero no se puede descartar por completo, ya que el ganado y los patos utilizan cuernos y picos para descargar el exceso de calor A pesar de la cubierta del cuerno.

facts.statement: Published descriptions of Hesperosaurus contradict each other due to changes and differences in interpretation.
facts.quote: Las diversas descripciones publicadas de Hesperosaurus se contradicen entre sí debido a los cambios y diferencias en la interpretación.

facts.statement: In 2001, it represented the oldest known stegosaur in the United States.
facts.quote: En 2001, representaba al más antiguo estegosaurio estadounidense conocido.

facts.statement: The skeleton was partially articulated and, based on healed fractures, belonged to an adult individual.
facts.quote: El esqueleto estaba parcialmente articulado y, en vista de las fracturas curadas, pertenece a un individuo adulto.

facts.statement: Specimen SMA 0018, nicknamed "Victory," was discovered between 1996 and 1997 at the Howe-Stephens quarry in Big Horn County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: Entre 1996 y 1997, se descubrió el espécimen SMA 0018, también denominado erróneamente SMA V03, apodado "Victory" por la sensación de victoria que sintió el equipo explorador cuando descubrieron el Allosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2009, specimens nicknamed "Moritz" and "Lilly" were initially reclassified as Hesperosaurus mjosi cf.
facts.quote: En 2009, inicialmente solo "Moritz" y "Lilly" se reclasificaron como Hesperosaurus mjosi cf.

facts.statement: In 2010, the specimen nicknamed "Victoria" was referred to Hesperosaurus mjosi by Nicolai Christiansen and Emanuel Tschopp.
facts.quote: En 2010, "Victoria" fue referida a Hesperosaurus mjosi por Nicolai Christiansen y Emanuel Tschopp.

facts.statement: In 2015, additional specimens were reported, including a concentration of at least five individuals found at the JRDI 5ES quarry near Grass Range, Montana.
facts.quote: En 2015, se informaron especímenes adicionales, una concentración de al menos cinco individuos descubiertos en la cantera JRDI 5ES cerca de Grass Range, Montana y dos individuos encontrados en la cantera Meilyn en Como Bluff.

facts.statement: A new specimen of H. mjosi from Montana was described in 2018.
facts.quote: En 2018, se describió un nuevo espécimen de H. mjosi de Montana.

facts.statement: Kenneth Carpenter originally concluded that Hesperosaurus was a fairly basal stegosaurid.
facts.quote: Carpenter había concluido originalmente que Hesperosaurus era un estegosáurido bastante basal.

facts.statement: In 2008, Susannah Maidment and colleagues published an extensive phylogenetic study that recovered Hesperosaurus as a derived form closely related to Stegosaurus and Wuerhosaurus.
facts.quote: Susannah Maidment y sus colegas en 2008 publicaron un estudio filogenético más extenso en el que se recuperó como una forma derivada, estrechamente relacionada con Stegosaurus y Wuerhosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2010, Carpenter rejected the synonymy of Hesperosaurus with Stegosaurus, arguing that Hesperosaurus was sufficiently different to be named a separate genus.
facts.quote: Carpenter, considerando el problema más de una naturaleza filosófica que científica, rechazó en 2010 la sinonimia de Hesperosaurus con Stegosaurus, afirmando que, en su opinión, Hesperosaurus era lo suficientemente diferente de Stegosaurus para ser nombrado un género separado.

facts.statement: In 2017, Raven and Maidment recognized both Miragaia and Hesperosaurus as distinct genera from Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2017, Raven y Maidment reconocieron tanto a Miragaia como a Hesperosaurus como géneros distintos de Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: Extensive phylogenetic studies by Maidment recovered Hesperosaurus as a highly derived stegosaurid and the sister species of Wuerhosaurus.
facts.quote: Estudios filogenéticos más extensos realizados por Maidment recuperaron Hesperosaurus como un estegosáurido muy derivado y la especie hermana de Wuerhosaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Hesperosaurus is Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Stegosaurinae

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus belongs to the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Hesperosaurus lived during the early Kimmeridgian, approximately 156 million years ago.
facts.quote: que data del Kimmeridgiense temprano, aproximadamente 156 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an almost complete skull and much of the skeleton, including thirteen neck vertebrae, thirteen posterior vertebrae, three sacral vertebrae, forty-four tail vertebrae, dorsal ribs, chevrons, a complete pelvis, and ten plates from the neck and back.
facts.quote: Consiste en un cráneo casi completo y gran parte del esqueleto. Incluye los elementos desarticulados del cráneo, las mandíbulas inferiores posteriores, un hioides, trece vértebras del cuello, trece vértebras traseras, tres sacros, cuarenta y cuatro vértebras de la cola, costillas del cuello, costillas dorsales, cheurones, una escapula del hombro izquierdo, una pelvis completa, tendones osificados y diez placas del cuello y la espalda.

facts.statement: Plates found at the quarry came in two types: one taller and one shorter.
facts.quote: Las placas encontradas en la cantera venían en dos tipos, una más alta y otra más baja.

facts.statement: Saitta suggested that tall plates typified females, while males were equipped with short plates.
facts.quote: Saitta sugirió que las placas altas tipificaban a las hembras, mientras que los machos estaban equipados con placas bajas.

facts.statement: The findings of the study were questioned by paleontologists Kevin Padian and Kenneth Carpenter, although no formal scientific studies were published as refutation.
facts.quote: Los hallazgos del estudio fueron cuestionados por los paleontólogos Kevin Padian.y Kenneth Carpenter, aunque no se publicaron estudios científicos formales como refutación.
